cities.name: Sydney
cities.tagline: Harbour city of beaches, ferries, and sandstone headlands
cities.general: Sydney wraps a world-famous harbour with surf beaches, coastal walks, ferry rides, and national-park headlands. It is the natural starting point for east-coast journeys, Blue Mountains day trips, and food-led city stays.

Walk from Bondi to Coogee

Catch a CityCat ferry
Visit QAGOMA
Plan a hinterland day trip

cities.tagline: Indian Ocean beaches, Swan River sunsets, and Rottnest escapes

Explore Fremantle's markets and heritage streets
Ride a ferry to Rottnest Island

Taste wine in the Adelaide Hills
Ride the tram to Glenelg
Plan a Kangaroo Island side trip

cities.name: Alice Springs
cities.tagline: Red Centre town for desert ranges and Larapinta Trail access
cities.general: Alice Springs is the practical hub of Australia's Red Centre, backed by the MacDonnell Ranges and the Larapinta Trail. It works best for self-drive desert trips, Aboriginal art, and outback landscapes.

Visit the Alice Springs Desert Park
Drive the West MacDonnell Ranges
Browse local Aboriginal art galleries

cities.tagline: Harbour city of volcanic cones, islands, and Pacific food

Take a ferry to Waiheke Island
Walk the waterfront and Wynyard Quarter
Explore west-coast beaches

cities.tagline: Compact capital of harbour hills, cafes, museums, and film craft

Ride the cable car to the Botanic Garden
Walk the Mount Victoria lookout
Tour Weta Workshop
tips: Wind is part of the experience; pack a shell

cities.name: Christchurch
cities.tagline: Garden city rebuilt with creativity and Canterbury access

Visit Riverside Market
Ride the tram loop

cities.name: Queenstown
cities.tagline: Alpine lake base for adventure, wine, and Great Walks

Cruise or drive Lake Wakatipu

cities.tagline: Geothermal lakes, Maori culture, and forest trails

cities.tagline: Southern heritage city with wildlife-rich Otago Peninsula

Look for albatross and penguins on Otago Peninsula
Walk Tunnel Beach
Explore local breweries and cafes

cities.tagline: Sunny arts town near Abel Tasman beaches and alpine parks
cities.general: Nelson is a sunny South Island base for galleries, markets, wineries, Abel Tasman beaches, and inland alpine parks. It works well for slower coastal travel and Great Walk logistics.

Taste wine around Moutere or Mapua
Day-trip into Abel Tasman
Walk to the Centre of New Zealand viewpoint
tips: Summer accommodation fills early

cities.name: Wanaka
cities.tagline: Lakeside mountain town for day hikes and Mount Aspiring access

Explore Chinatown and pearling history
Visit Gantheaume Point
Use Broome as a Kimberley road-trip base

hikes.name: Overland Track
hikes.tagline: 65 km alpine traverse from Cradle Mountain to Lake St Clair
hikes.summary: The Overland Track is Tasmania's signature multi-day walk, crossing alpine moorland, dolerite peaks, rainforest, waterfalls, and glacial lakes between Cradle Mountain and Lake St Clair.
tips: Bookings are required in the main walking season
Carry full wet-weather gear even in summer
Side trips add time and exposure
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers start at Ronny Creek near Cradle Mountain and finish at Lake St Clair, using booked huts or tent platforms along the route.

tips: Walk in the cooler months from May to September
Water logistics define each stage
Avoid exposed climbs during heat
hikes.start_instructions: Traditional east-to-west itineraries begin at Alice Springs Telegraph Station and finish with an early climb of Mount Sonder.

hikes.name: Cape to Cape Track
hikes.tagline: Coastal walk between Cape Naturaliste and Cape Leeuwin
hikes.summary: The Cape to Cape Track follows limestone cliffs, beaches, karri forest pockets, and surf breaks along Western Australia's Margaret River coast.
tips: Soft sand sections are tiring
Wildflowers peak in spring
Arrange end-to-end transport before starting
hikes.start_instructions: Walkers usually start at either lighthouse; north-to-south itineraries finish at Cape Leeuwin near Augusta.

hikes.tagline: Clifftop and beach walk from Apollo Bay to the Twelve Apostles
hikes.summary: The Great Ocean Walk threads forests, beaches, river mouths, campsites, and limestone cliffs along Victoria's famous shipwreck coast.
tips: Check tide times for beach sections
Pre-book campsites or luggage transfers
Weather can be windy on exposed headlands
hikes.start_instructions: The official route starts at Apollo Bay and heads west toward the Twelve Apostles visitor area.

hikes.name: Six Foot Track
hikes.tagline: Historic Blue Mountains track from Katoomba to Jenolan Caves
hikes.summary: The Six Foot Track follows an 1880s bridle route through gullies, farmland, suspension bridges, and ridgelines between Katoomba and Jenolan Caves.
tips: Carry water between camps
Check Jenolan road access before arranging pickup
Expect steep climbs out of valleys
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers begin near Katoomba's Explorers Tree and arrange transport from Jenolan Caves.

hikes.name: Routeburn Track
hikes.tagline: Alpine Great Walk between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland
hikes.summary: The Routeburn Track crosses beech forest, waterfalls, alpine tarns, and the Harris Saddle between the Queenstown and Te Anau sides of the Southern Alps.
tips: Huts book out quickly
Transport is needed between trailheads
Snow and avalanche hazards affect shoulder seasons
hikes.start_instructions: Walkers commonly start at Routeburn Shelter near Glenorchy and finish at The Divide on the Milford Road.

hikes.name: Milford Track
hikes.tagline: Classic Fiordland Great Walk to Milford Sound
hikes.summary: The Milford Track follows lake, river, rainforest, and alpine pass terrain from Lake Te Anau toward Milford Sound, including Mackinnon Pass and Sutherland Falls side trips.
tips: Great Walk bookings sell out fast
Heavy rain can flood sections
Boat and bus transfers are part of the route
hikes.start_instructions: The managed walk starts with a boat transfer to Glade Wharf and finishes with a boat from Sandfly Point near Milford Sound.

hikes.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
hikes.tagline: Volcanic day walk past crater lakes and lava fields
hikes.summary: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing traverses exposed volcanic terrain between Mangatepopo and Ketetahi, with crater rims, emerald lakes, steam vents, and huge plateau views.
tips: Use shuttle transport; parking is restricted
Go only in suitable weather
Winter conditions require alpine gear and experience
hikes.start_instructions: Most hikers use shuttle services from National Park or Turangi to start at Mangatepopo and finish at Ketetahi.

hikes.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track
hikes.tagline: Beach-hopping Great Walk with tidal crossings and water taxis
hikes.summary: The Abel Tasman Coast Track links golden beaches, forested headlands, estuaries, and campsites along one of New Zealand's sunniest coastlines.
tips: Time tidal crossings carefully
Water taxis make flexible section walks possible
Book huts and campsites in summer
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers begin at Marahau and use water taxis or road transport around the northern trailhead.

hikes.name: Kepler Track
hikes.tagline: Fiordland circuit of lake shore, beech forest, and alpine ridges
hikes.summary: The Kepler Track is a purpose-built Fiordland circuit from near Te Anau, climbing from lakeshore forest to long alpine ridge walking and descending through wetlands.
tips: Alpine sections are exposed to wind
Huts require Great Walk bookings
The track can be shortened with transport to control gates
hikes.start_instructions: The usual circuit starts near Te Anau at the Kepler Track car park or control gates.

hikes.name: Hooker Valley Track
hikes.tagline: Glacial valley walk to Aoraki Mount Cook viewpoints
hikes.summary: The Hooker Valley Track is an accessible out-and-back walk from White Horse Hill to swing bridges, glacier views, and Aoraki Mount Cook framed above Hooker Lake.
tips: Start early for calmer weather and parking
Stay on marked boardwalks
Cloud can hide Aoraki quickly
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the White Horse Hill campground and follow the signed valley track to Hooker Lake.

hikes.name: Three Capes Track
hikes.tagline: Clifftop Tasman Peninsula walk with dolerite sea stacks
hikes.summary: The Three Capes Track follows the Tasman Peninsula's dramatic sea cliffs, heathland, coastal forest, and dolerite columns between Cape Pillar and Cape Hauy.
tips: Bookings are required for the hut-based itinerary
Weather can be windy and exposed
Carry layers even in summer
hikes.start_instructions: The managed walk starts from Port Arthur with transport and finishes near Fortescue Bay.

photos.caption: The geography of South Australia; historical, physical, political & commercial

hikes.name: Bibbulmun Track
hikes.tagline: Western Australia end-to-end walk from Perth hills to Albany
hikes.summary: The Bibbulmun Track traverses jarrah, karri, tingle forest, farmland, rivers, and wild southern coastline between Kalamunda and Albany.
tips: End-to-end walkers need careful food drops
Spring wildflowers are a highlight
Huts are basic and first-come, first-served
hikes.start_instructions: The northern terminus is in Kalamunda near Perth; the southern terminus is in Albany.

hikes.name: Heysen Trail
hikes.tagline: South Australian traverse from Cape Jervis to the Flinders Ranges
hikes.summary: The Heysen Trail links beaches, vineyards, forests, farmland, and rugged ranges from the Fleurieu Peninsula to Parachilna Gorge.
tips: Northern sections close during fire danger season
Water and resupply planning are essential
Walk cooler months for exposed range country
hikes.start_instructions: Most section walkers choose shorter legs; end-to-end hikers usually walk north in cooler months.

hikes.name: Australian Alps Walking Track
hikes.tagline: High-country traverse through Victoria, New South Wales, and ACT
hikes.summary: The Australian Alps Walking Track links alpine national parks, snow gums, ridgelines, huts, and remote high-country terrain from Walhalla to Canberra.
tips: Navigation and self-sufficiency are required
Snow can persist on high sections
Food drops simplify long remote stretches
hikes.start_instructions: The official route runs between Walhalla in Victoria and Tharwa near Canberra.

Walk in the dry season
Heat and water planning matter every day

hikes.summary: The Thorsborne Trail crosses Hinchinbrook Island's beaches, mangroves, rainforest, creeks, and mountain views between Ramsay Bay and George Point.

Tide timing affects creek and beach sections
Pack for wet tropical conditions

Carry sun and wind protection
Snow changes the route in winter and spring

Steps are steep in places
Continue to the beach only if you have extra time

Swim only at patrolled beaches
Public buses connect both ends

Carry water through exposed sections
Check train and ferry connections

hikes.name: Grand Canyon Walk
hikes.tagline: Historic loop through rainforest canyon near Blackheath
hikes.summary: The Grand Canyon Walk descends from Blue Mountains lookouts into fern-filled slot canyon, waterfalls, and rainforest before climbing back to Evans Lookout.

Carry a warm layer in the canyon
Start early on weekends
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Evans Lookout near Blackheath and follow the signed loop.

hikes.tagline: Rainforest, beaches, lighthouse views, and Australia's easternmost point
hikes.summary: The Cape Byron Walking Track loops from Byron Bay through rainforest, beaches, cliffs, the lighthouse, and Australia's easternmost mainland point.
tips: Parking near the lighthouse is limited
Whales pass in season
Carry water in humid weather
hikes.start_instructions: Start near Captain Cook Lookout or Byron Bay beach and follow the signed loop.

hikes.name: Grampians Peaks Trail
hikes.tagline: Gariwerd ridgeline traverse of sandstone peaks and cultural landscapes
hikes.summary: The Grampians Peaks Trail links rugged sandstone ridges, lookouts, waterfalls, camps, and Gariwerd cultural landscapes across western Victoria.
tips: Book designated campsites
Water availability varies by section
Weather is exposed on ridges
hikes.start_instructions: The full route runs north to south from Mount Zero to Dunkeld.

hikes.name: Wilsons Promontory Southern Circuit
hikes.tagline: Remote beaches, granite peaks, and southern mainland wilderness
hikes.summary: The Wilsons Promontory Southern Circuit links Tidal River, Sealers Cove, Refuge Cove, Waterloo Bay, and remote granite-backed beaches.
tips: Campsites require booking
Tide and weather affect beach walking
Carry reliable wet-weather gear
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Tidal River and follow the signed overnight circuit.

hikes.name: Light to Light Walk
hikes.tagline: Ben Boyd coastal walk between Boyds Tower and Green Cape
hikes.summary: The Light to Light Walk follows red coastal rock, heath, beaches, and historic ruins between Boyds Tower and Green Cape Lightstation.
tips: Campsites should be booked
Weather is exposed
Check park alerts for fire or storms
hikes.start_instructions: Most walkers start at Boyds Tower south of Eden and finish at Green Cape.

hikes.name: Dove Lake Circuit
hikes.tagline: Boardwalk and lakeshore loop under Cradle Mountain
hikes.summary: The Dove Lake Circuit is an accessible loop of boardwalk, lakeshore, and rainforest beneath Cradle Mountain.
tips: Start early for parking
Weather changes quickly
Stay on boardwalks to protect vegetation
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Dove Lake car park after the Cradle Mountain shuttle.

hikes.name: The Pinnacle Walk
hikes.tagline: Stepped sandstone climb to the Halls Gap viewpoint
hikes.summary: The Pinnacle Walk climbs from Halls Gap through Wonderland sandstone to a classic Gariwerd lookout.
tips: Start early in heat
Rock is slippery after rain
Carry water on the climb
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Wonderland car park above Halls Gap.

hikes.name: Mount Gower Track
hikes.tagline: Guided cloudforest climb on Lord Howe Island
hikes.summary: The Mount Gower Track is a guided climb through palm forest and cloudforest to the summit of Lord Howe Island.
tips: A licensed guide is required
The walk is long and exposed in places
Book well ahead
hikes.start_instructions: Guided groups start from the southern settlement end of Lord Howe Island.

hikes.name: Kings Canyon Rim Walk
hikes.tagline: Red sandstone rim circuit above Watarrka's canyon floor
hikes.summary: The Kings Canyon Rim Walk climbs steeply then circuits the canyon rim past the Garden of Eden and sheer red walls.
tips: Start at dawn in warm months
Carry more water than you think
The first climb is the steepest
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed rim-walk car park in Watarrka National Park.

hikes.name: Dales Gorge Walk
hikes.tagline: Karijini gorge loop of Fortescue Falls, Fern Pool, and rim views
hikes.summary: The Dales Gorge Walk links Fortescue Falls, Fern Pool, and a rim return through Karijini's red banded iron formations.
tips: Steps are steep
Pools may close after rain
Carry water and sun protection
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Dales Gorge day-use car park in Karijini National Park.

hikes.name: Cape Otway Lightstation Walk
hikes.tagline: Coastal woodland walk to the Otway lighthouse
hikes.summary: A short Great Otway walk through coastal woodland to Cape Otway Lightstation, with koala habitat and shipwreck-coast views.
tips: Lighthouse entry is ticketed
Koalas are often in roadside trees
Weather is changeable
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Cape Otway Lightstation car park off the Great Ocean Road.

hikes.name: Fitzroy Falls East Rim Track
hikes.tagline: Plateau lookouts above Morton National Park's sandstone gorge
hikes.summary: The East Rim Track follows the plateau edge from Fitzroy Falls visitor centre past multiple gorge lookouts.
tips: Boardwalks can be slippery
Stay behind fences
Combine with the west rim if time allows
hikes.start_instructions: Start at the Fitzroy Falls visitor centre in Morton National Park.

hikes.name: Border Track
hikes.tagline: Lamington plateau rainforest walk between O'Reilly's and Binna Burra
hikes.summary: The Border Track crosses Lamington's rainforest plateau between O'Reilly's and Binna Burra through World Heritage forest.
tips: Leeches are common after rain
Carry a headlamp for late finishes
Transport is needed between ends
hikes.start_instructions: Walkers usually start at O'Reilly's Green Mountains and finish at Binna Burra.

hikes.name: Toolona Creek Circuit
hikes.tagline: Waterfall gorge and Antarctic beech circuit from O'Reilly's
hikes.summary: The Toolona Creek Circuit follows a rainforest gorge of waterfalls before returning along the Border Track through Antarctic beech.
tips: The gorge is slippery
Start early
Carry leech protection after rain
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed circuit at O'Reilly's Green Mountains.

hikes.name: Wollumbin Summit Track
hikes.tagline: Steep rainforest climb of the Tweed volcanic plug
hikes.summary: The Wollumbin Summit Track climbs steep rainforest and rock to the remnant volcanic plug of the Tweed caldera.
tips: Check current access and cultural guidance before going
The climb is steep and slippery
Start before dawn for sunrise
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed national-park car park if the summit track is open.

hikes.name: Frenchman Peak Walk
hikes.tagline: Steep granite climb above Cape Le Grand's white beaches
hikes.summary: The Frenchman Peak Walk climbs a granite dome above Cape Le Grand for views of Lucky Bay, Thistle Cove, and the Recherche islands.
tips: Rock is steep and exposed
Start early
Carry water and sun protection
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed car park inside Cape Le Grand National Park.

hikes.name: Bluff Knoll Walk
hikes.tagline: Stirling Range summit climb through cloud-forest heath
hikes.summary: The Bluff Knoll Walk climbs the Stirling Range's best-known peak through heath and cloud-prone slopes to a wide southern-ocean view.
tips: Weather closes in quickly
Carry warm layers even in summer
Dieback hygiene stations must be used
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Bluff Knoll car park in Stirling Range National Park.

hikes.name: Tarn Shelf Track
hikes.tagline: Alpine lakes and pandani above Mount Field's plateau
hikes.summary: The Tarn Shelf Track visits alpine lakes, pandani, and ski-field country above Mount Field, often combined with Lake Webster or Rodway Hut.
tips: Snow is possible in any season
Boardwalks are icy in winter
Start from Lake Dobson
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Lake Dobson at the top of the Mount Field road.

hikes.name: Russell Falls Walk
hikes.tagline: Short rainforest walk to Tasmania's most famous waterfall
hikes.summary: The Russell Falls Walk is an easy rainforest path from Mount Field visitor centre to the three-tier waterfall.
tips: The path is popular and easy
Continue to Horseshoe Falls if time allows
Winter spray is cold
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Mount Field visitor centre car park.

hikes.name: Spit Bridge to Manly Walk
hikes.tagline: Harbour bushland walk from The Spit to Manly Wharf
hikes.summary: The Spit to Manly Walk follows Sydney Harbour through bushland, coves, Clontarf, and headlands to Manly Wharf.
tips: Go at low tide for some rock sections
Buses or ferries connect both ends
Carry water on hot days
hikes.start_instructions: Start at the northern end of Spit Bridge and follow the signed harbour track.

hikes.name: Manly Scenic Walkway
hikes.tagline: North Head and harbour-edge walk from Manly
hikes.summary: The Manly Scenic Walkway links harbour coves, North Head views, and coastal bushland around the Manly peninsula.
tips: Sections can be walked separately
North Head is exposed to wind
Combine with the ferry
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Manly Wharf and follow signs toward North Head or The Spit.

hikes.name: Cape Hauy Track
hikes.tagline: Dolerite cliffs and sea stacks at the end of the Three Capes country
hikes.summary: The Cape Hauy Track runs from Fortescue Bay through coastal heath to one of Tasmania's most dramatic dolerite lookouts.
tips: The last lookout is exposed
Carry layers
Add time if combining with Fortescue Bay swimming
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Fortescue Bay car park on the Tasman Peninsula.

hikes.name: Hinchinbrook Lookout Walk
hikes.tagline: Short Cardwell-range lookout toward Hinchinbrook Island
hikes.summary: A short hinterland walk to a lookout over the Hinchinbrook Channel and island massif near Cardwell.
tips: The road is winding
Carry water
Cassowaries may be on nearby roads
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed lookout car park west of Cardwell.

hikes.name: Mount Kosciuszko Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: High-country walk from Thredbo or Charlotte Pass to Australia's summit
hikes.summary: The Kosciuszko Summit Walk crosses alpine herbfields and metal walkway to the highest point on the Australian mainland.
tips: Weather can be severe in any season
The Thredbo chairlift shortens the walk
Carry sun and wind protection
hikes.start_instructions: Most summer walkers start from the top of the Thredbo Kosciuszko Express chairlift.

hikes.name: Mount Ngungun Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Short steep climb to the best Glass House Mountains viewpoint
hikes.summary: The Mount Ngungun Summit Walk is the most accessible Glass House Mountains climb, rising through woodland to a rocky summit with views of Beerwah, Tibrogargan, and Coonowrin.
tips: Rock is slippery after rain
Start early on weekends
Carry water; the climb is short but steep
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed Ngungun car park off Fullertons Road.

hikes.name: Mount Tibrogargan Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Exposed volcanic-plug scramble above Beerwah township
hikes.summary: The Tibrogargan Summit Walk climbs steep rock on the crouching-gorilla plug, with exposure, loose sections, and wide hinterland views.
tips: Not a beginner walk
Avoid in rain or high wind
Check current park access before climbing
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Tibrogargan day-use area off Marshs Road.

hikes.name: Mount Beerwah Walk
hikes.tagline: Steep climb of the highest Glass House Mountains plug
hikes.summary: The Mount Beerwah Walk is a steep volcanic-plug climb from the western trailhead, with rock slabs, exposure, and summit views across the Sunshine Coast hinterland.
tips: Confirm the track is open; access has been restricted at times
Rock slabs are dangerous when wet
This is a serious short climb, not a stroll
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Mount Beerwah car park west of the peak if the summit route is open.

hikes.name: Tibrogargan Circuit
hikes.tagline: Easy woodland loop around the base of Mount Tibrogargan
hikes.summary: The Tibrogargan Circuit is a mostly easy loop around the base of the plug, with changing views of the cliff faces and nearby peaks.
tips: Good alternative if the summit is closed or too exposed
Carry water in summer
Trailhead parking fills on weekends
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Tibrogargan day-use area and follow the signed circuit.

hikes.name: Kondalilla Falls Circuit
hikes.tagline: Steep rainforest descent to the waterfall and swimming hole
hikes.summary: The Kondalilla Falls Circuit drops from the Blackall Range picnic area through rainforest to the waterfall and rock pools, then climbs back to the escarpment.
tips: The return climb is steep
Rocks around the pool are slippery
Start early on hot days
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Kondalilla National Park picnic area near Montville.

hikes.name: Mount Coolum Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Steep coastal-plug climb above Coolum Beach
hikes.summary: The Mount Coolum Summit Walk climbs the rhyolite plug from Tanah Street West, with a short, steep pad to a broad summit and views along the Sunshine Coast.
tips: Start early; the slope has little shade
Rock is slippery after rain
Parking on Tanah Street fills quickly
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed trailhead on Tanah Street West, Mount Coolum.

hikes.name: Mount Tinbeerwah Lookout Walk
hikes.tagline: Short hinterland climb to a Noosa-coast lookout
hikes.summary: The Mount Tinbeerwah walk climbs from the sealed lookout road to a summit platform with views over lakes, forest, and the Noosa coast.
tips: The last rock steps are steep
Go early for clearer views
Combine with Tewantin or Noosa
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Mount Tinbeerwah car park off Tinbeerwah Road.

hikes.name: Mount Cooroora Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Steep rocky climb from Pomona to the Cooroora plug
hikes.summary: The Mount Cooroora Summit Walk rises directly from Pomona through woodland and rock to a sharp volcanic summit above the Noosa hinterland.
tips: A serious short climb with exposure
Avoid in rain
Carry water
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed trailhead on Reserve Street in Pomona.

hikes.name: Mount Barney South Ridge
hikes.tagline: Classic steep route to South East Queensland's biggest peak
hikes.summary: The South Ridge route is the usual walkers' line on Mount Barney, climbing from Yellow Pinch through open forest and steep rock to East Peak.
tips: Start before dawn in summer
Carry 3+ litres of water
The descent is hard on knees and navigation
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Yellow Pinch car park and follow the South Ridge / Peasants Ridge signs.

hikes.name: Bartle Frere Western Summit Track
hikes.tagline: Queensland's highest mountain through Wet Tropics rainforest
hikes.summary: The western Bartle Frere track climbs from Josephine Falls / Broken Nose country through rainforest, boulders, and cloud forest to Queensland's highest summit.
tips: This is a long, wet, and serious day
Leeches and cloud are normal
Carry a map; the top can be socked in
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the western Bartle Frere trailhead near Josephine Falls / Broken Nose access.

hikes.name: Walshs Pyramid Walk
hikes.tagline: Steep standalone climb south of Cairns
hikes.summary: Walshs Pyramid is a relentless grassy and rocky climb from Gordonvale's southern flats to a sharp summit with Wet Tropics and coast views.
tips: Almost no shade
Start at first light
Carry more water than the distance suggests
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed car park on the Gordonvale–Gillies side of the peak.

hikes.name: Mount Coot-tha Summit Track
hikes.tagline: Brisbane lookout mountain from the botanic gardens
hikes.summary: The Mount Coot-tha tracks climb from the botanic gardens and JC Slaughter Falls to the summit lookout above Brisbane.
tips: Weekends are busy
Go early for clearer views
The summit lookout has traffic; the tracks are quieter
hikes.start_instructions: Start from JC Slaughter Falls or the botanic gardens and follow summit-track signs.

hikes.name: Mount Feathertop via Bungalow Spur
hikes.tagline: Victoria's classic hut-and-summit climb from Harrietville
hikes.summary: Bungalow Spur is the standard walkers' route to Mount Feathertop, climbing from Harrietville through forest to Federation Hut and the exposed summit ridge.
tips: Start before dawn
The summit ridge is dangerous in high wind or snow
Carry an emergency layer even in summer
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Feathertop Track car park on Feathertop Track, Harrietville.

hikes.name: Mount Bogong via Staircase Spur
hikes.tagline: Victoria's highest mountain from Mountain Creek
hikes.summary: Staircase Spur is the classic Mount Bogong route, climbing from Mountain Creek through mountain ash to Bivouac Hut and the exposed high plains summit.
tips: Alpine weather kills; turn back if it closes in
Start early
Snow and ice linger into spring
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Mountain Creek campground and follow Staircase Spur signs.

hikes.name: The Horn Walk Mount Buffalo
hikes.tagline: Short granite climb to the highest point on Mount Buffalo
hikes.summary: The Horn Walk crosses snow-gum woodland and granite slabs to the highest point of the Mount Buffalo plateau, with views over the Ovens Valley.
tips: The last slabs are exposed in wind
Ice is common in winter
Combine with the Gorge and Lake Catani
hikes.start_instructions: Drive the plateau road to The Horn car park and take the signed walk.

hikes.name: Mount Macedon Memorial Cross Walk
hikes.tagline: Forest walk to the Memorial Cross above the Macedon Ranges
hikes.summary: The Mount Macedon walk climbs through cool forest to the Memorial Cross and lookout, with views across the volcanic plains toward Melbourne.
tips: The cross precinct can be busy on weekends
Fog is common
Combine with Sanatorium Lake
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed Macedon Ranges walks near the Memorial Cross road.

hikes.name: Mount William Walk
hikes.tagline: Highest Grampians peak from the sealed summit road
hikes.summary: The Mount William walk uses the sealed access road and a short summit pad to the highest peak in Gariwerd / the Grampians, with wide western-district views.
tips: The top is cold and windy
Cloud can wipe the view
The road is steep; walkers share it with cars
hikes.start_instructions: Drive the Mount William Road to the upper car park and walk the summit track.

hikes.name: Didthul / Pigeon House Mountain Walk
hikes.tagline: Sandstone peak with ladders to a Morton National Park summit
hikes.summary: The Didthul walk climbs from Yadboro country through forest and sandstone to steel ladders and a small summit with coast and Budawang views.
tips: The ladders are steep
Start early; the last kilometres of road are unsealed
Carry water
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Pigeon House Mountain car park off Yadboro Road.

hikes.name: Mount Solitary Walk
hikes.tagline: Blue Mountains ridge above the Jamison Valley
hikes.summary: The Mount Solitary walk drops from the Golden Stairs or Katoomba cliffs, crosses the Ruined Castle saddle, and climbs the solitary ridge above the valley floor.
tips: This is a long, steep day
Carry a light; the descent is slow
Check fire-season closures
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Golden Stairs car park on Glenraphael Drive, Katoomba.

hikes.name: Mount Kaputar Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Short high-country walk to the Nandewar Range summit
hikes.summary: The Mount Kaputar summit walk is a short high-plateau stroll from the road to the lookout on the Nandewar Range above Narrabri.
tips: The access road is long and winding
It can be cold even in summer
Watch for ice in winter
hikes.start_instructions: Drive the Mount Kaputar road to the summit car park.

hikes.name: St Mary Peak Circuit
hikes.tagline: Highest walk in Ikara / Wilpena Pound
hikes.summary: The St Mary Peak circuit climbs from Wilpena through Tanderra Saddle to Ngarri Mudlanha, then returns around the pound rim with huge Flinders views.
tips: Walk in the cooler months
Carry a lot of water
The outer loop is long and exposed
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Wilpena visitor centre and follow Tanderra Saddle / St Mary Peak signs.

hikes.name: Mount Lofty Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Adelaide Hills climb from Waterfall Gully to the summit lookout
hikes.summary: The Waterfall Gully to Mount Lofty walk is Adelaide's staple mountain path, climbing beside First Falls and through stringybark forest to the summit lookout.
tips: Start early on weekends
The sealed path is steep
Carry water in summer
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Waterfall Gully car park and follow the Mount Lofty Summit track.

hikes.name: Mount Remarkable Summit Hike
hikes.tagline: Southern Flinders climb from Melrose
hikes.summary: The Mount Remarkable summit hike climbs from Melrose through forest and steep ridgeline to the highest point of the southern Flinders.
tips: Start early
The ridge is exposed
Carry extra water
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed trailhead in Melrose.

hikes.name: Toolbrunup Peak Walk
hikes.tagline: Steep Stirling Range scramble near Bluff Knoll
hikes.summary: Toolbrunup is a steep, rocky Stirling Range climb with loose gullies and a sharp summit, shorter than Bluff Knoll but more technical.
tips: Not a beginner walk
Rockfall is a risk
Avoid in wet or high wind
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Toolbrunup car park on Stirling Range Drive.

hikes.name: Castle Rock and Granite Skywalk
hikes.tagline: Granite castle and skywalk in the Porongurup Range
hikes.summary: The Castle Rock walk climbs through karri and granite to the Granite Skywalk platform on the Porongurup Range east of Albany.
tips: The skywalk is exposed
Rock is slippery when wet
Start early for parking
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Castle Rock car park in Porongurup National Park.

hikes.name: Mount Augustus Summit Loop
hikes.tagline: Long hot climb of Burringurrah in the Gascoyne
hikes.summary: The Mount Augustus summit loop is a long exposed walk up the sandstone monocline, with gorge views and a huge Gascoyne horizon.
tips: Walk in the cooler months only
Start before sunrise
Carry more water than you think you need
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the signed summit car park inside Mount Augustus National Park.

hikes.name: Mount Sonder Lookout Walk
hikes.tagline: Larapinta western high point above the Redbank valley
hikes.summary: The Mount Sonder walk climbs from Redbank Gorge along the Larapinta's last ridge to Rwetyepme, often done for sunrise over the West MacDonnells.
tips: Start in the dark for sunrise
There is little shade
Carry a lot of water
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Redbank Gorge car park at the western end of the Larapinta Trail.

hikes.name: Frenchmans Cap Track
hikes.tagline: Western Tasmania quartzite dome from Lake Tahune
hikes.summary: The Frenchmans Cap Track crosses the Loddon Plains and climbs to Lake Tahune hut, then a steep quartzite pad to one of Tasmania's most striking summits.
tips: The Loddon can be a mud slog
Book or carry a tent for Tahune
The summit is dangerous in ice and high wind
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Frenchmans Cap trackhead on the Lyell Highway west of Derwent Bridge.

hikes.name: Mount Ossa Side Trip
hikes.tagline: Tasmania's highest mountain from Pelion Gap
hikes.summary: The Mount Ossa side trip leaves the Overland Track at Pelion Gap and climbs dolerite toward Tasmania's highest summit, often combined with Pelion West views.
tips: Only in stable weather
The upper rock is exposed
This is a side trip, not a shortcut
hikes.start_instructions: Leave the Overland Track at Pelion Gap and follow the Mount Ossa pad.

hikes.name: Hartz Peak Walk
hikes.tagline: Dolerite summit above Hartz Lake in southern Tasmania
hikes.summary: The Hartz Peak walk follows boardwalk and alpine pad from the Hartz Mountains car park past lookouts and Lake Esperance to the rocky summit.
tips: Weather closes in fast
Boardwalks are icy in winter
Carry a jacket even in summer
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the Hartz Mountains National Park car park south of Geeveston.

hikes.name: Cradle Mountain Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Dolerite scramble from Dove Lake to the Cradle summit
hikes.summary: The Cradle Mountain summit walk leaves the Dove Lake circuit, climbs past Lake Wilks and the Face Track, and finishes on exposed dolerite to the summit.
tips: Turn back if the top is in cloud or ice
Start early from the Dove Lake shuttle
This is a scramble, not a staircase
hikes.start_instructions: Take the Dove Lake shuttle and follow Face Track / summit signs.

hikes.name: kunanyi / Mount Wellington Organ Pipes Walk
hikes.tagline: Alpine pad beneath the Organ Pipes above Hobart
hikes.summary: The Organ Pipes Walk traverses the dolerite columns on kunanyi / Mount Wellington, linking the Pinnacle area with Lost World and city views.
tips: Weather can be wintery in any month
Rockfall occurs under the pipes
Carry a layer even if Hobart is warm
hikes.start_instructions: Start from The Springs or the Pinnacle and follow Organ Pipes Track signs.

hikes.name: Mount Canobolas Summit Walk
hikes.tagline: Short volcanic summit above Orange
hikes.summary: The Mount Canobolas walk is a short climb to the highest point of the central tablelands, with lookouts over Orange and the western slopes.
tips: It can be cold and windy
Combine with Federal Falls
The access road is winding
hikes.start_instructions: Start from the picnic area on Mount Canobolas Road.

hikes.name: Breadknife and Grand High Tops Walk
hikes.tagline: Warrumbungle circuit to the rhyolite Breadknife
hikes.summary: The Grand High Tops walk climbs from Pincham through forest and volcanic walls to the Breadknife and ridge lookouts in Warrumbungle National Park.
tips: Start early in summer
